unit.title: Time (2)
unit.blurb: Finding how long things take in minutes and hours, finding start and end times, and reading simple timetables and calendars.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Find time intervals in minutes and hours and work out start and end times.

p: To find how long something takes, **count on** from the start time to the end time: from 2:40 to 3:15 is 20 minutes to 3:00 and 15 more: **35 minutes**.

lesson.t: Why we jump to the hour
p: There are 60 minutes in an hour, not 100. Jumping to the next o'clock first stops mistakes when the time goes past the hour.

lesson.q: A film starts at 2:40 and ends at 4:15. How long is it?

p: Jump from the start to the next o'clock.
Jump to the end time and add all the jumps.

options.fb: There are 60 minutes in an hour.

2:30 → 3:00 is 30 min, then 15 more.

p: A **timetable** shows when things happen. Read across a row to find a time.
To find how long a journey takes, subtract the start time from the end time.

lesson.t: Why timetables are in rows and columns
p: Each column is one journey and each row is one stop. Reading down a column follows one bus all the way.

lesson.q: A bus leaves the school at 8:10 and reaches the park at 8:35. How long is the journey?

p: Find the time interval between them.
Keep your finger on one row so you read the times for the same bus.

q.prompt: In the timetable, how many minutes does bus 1 take from Park to Shops?
Before you read on: a bus leaves at 9:10 and the journey takes 20 minutes. When does it arrive?

options.fb: Correct.
Add 20 minutes.
20 minutes, not 2 hours.
